subject: Bastion egress proxy: outbound IPs, firewall posture, and operational runbook
messages:
From: Nicole Rojas <nicole@greenwave.ai>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
Cc: ops+security@acme-health.com
Date: Fri, 28 Aug 2026 15:03:00 -0700
Subject: Private endpoint: outbound connectivity and TLS interception concerns

Tessa — thanks for taking this on. Quick summary of our ask: GreenWave is evaluating Redwood Private (VPC deployment) and we need a crisp answer on what outbound egress we must allow from our private connectors and runtime nodes. Security team specifics:

- We need a minimal, stable set of IPs/CIDRs for firewall allowlisting (for control plane telemetry, heartbeat, model artifact fetches, and license checks).
- Is a forward proxy/bastion egress pattern supported? If yes, can we terminate TLS at our proxy, or does that break any mTLS flows to Redwood control endpoints?
- What ports and SNI hostnames should we permit (we operate with strict TLS inspection and SNI allowlist).
- Any ephemeral ranges or dynamic CDN edges we should account for? We prefer deterministic addresses rather than domain-only allowlists.

Could you share a proposed rule set we can present to our auditors? If you have a short runbook for operating a customer-side egress proxy that preserves auditability and keeps model downloads functioning, that would be ideal.

Thanks,
Nicole Rojas
Director, Platform Security
GreenWave Health

Attachments: none

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
To: Nicole Rojas <nicole@greenwave.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 28 Aug 2026 17:10:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private endpoint: outbound connectivity and TLS interception concerns

Nicole — appreciate the clear list. Summary answer up front: yes, we support a customer-side egress proxy (bastion) pattern and a deterministic allowlist model. We recommend a customer-managed forward proxy/NAT at the edge that we call the "bastion egress proxy." Key constraints and recommendations follow — attached is a short runbook and a proposed CSV of IPs for allowlisting.

High-level constraints:
- Control plane communication (telemetry, heartbeat, usage metrics, license check-in) requires outbound HTTPS (443) to a small set of stable IPs. We DO NOT require interception of mTLS at the customer proxy for internal-to-control-plane auth; the runtime uses standard TLS to api.control.redwood.ai and validates server certs. Terminating TLS on your proxy is supported only if your proxy preserves SNI and re-establishes TLS to Redwood (i.e., TLS break-and-reencrypt). If you have strict mTLS between runtime and our control plane (customer-managed certs), we can provide instructions, but default flow is server-authenticated TLS only.

Recommended allowlist items (see attached egress-ip-list.csv for current authoritative list):
- 3 static IPv4 /32 addresses for control plane ingress (for telemetry + control): 34.202.10.12, 34.202.10.13, 34.202.10.14 (these are NAT egress IPs used by our control endpoints).
- 2 CIDR blocks for artifact downloads (model shards and container images): 52.44.128.0/24, 52.44.129.0/24.
- Port: 443 outbound for all flows.
- Hostnames/SNI: api.control.redwood.com, artifacts.redwoodcdn.com — allowlist these SNI names in your TLS inspection config.

On TLS interception:
- If you break TLS and re-encrypt, ensure SNI is preserved and the outgoing SNI to Redwood is api.control.redwood.com (our endpoint requires correct SNI for proper routing).
- If you perform certificate pinning or mTLS validation on the runtime side, please coordinate; we support client cert rotation but it is an opt-in integration (we'll need to exchange keys/certs ahead of onboarding).

Operational notes and fallbacks:
- We publish an egress IP set (CSV) and rotate with a 30-day notice window. For strict-regulated environments we can provide a signed manifest and rotation calendar.
- For customers that cannot accept domain-only allowlists, our Dedicated/Private offering can be pinned to a customer-specific egress NAT pool (enterprise add-on).
- Heartbeat freq: runtime pings control plane every 30s under normal load; ensure egress proxy permits short-lived TCP/TLS sessions without aggressive idle timeouts.

Next steps I propose:
1) We share the runbook and the attached CSV (attached).
2) GreenWave security reviews and confirms they can open the listed IPs/CIDRs (or requests enterprise pinned NAT).
3) We schedule a 30-min gating call to validate TLS inspection behavior against our test endpoints.

I've attached: bastion-proxy-arch.png (example topology), egress-ip-list.csv (proposed allowlist), egress-runbook-v1.pdf (short ops playbook).

—Tessa
Tessa Morgan
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 29 Aug 2026 09:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Private endpoint: outbound connectivity and TLS interception concerns

Looping in a quick internal note before the call with GreenWave next week. Things to confirm on our side:

- Ensure the artifacts CDN blocks provided are stable for at least 90 days; engineering to confirm origin/backing CDN (we currently front with a multi-region CDN but can reserve egress pool for enterprise).
- Add explicit guidance in runbook for SNI forwarding behavior on proxies. Some customer proxies force TLS SNI to the originally requested host, others rewrite; we should call out that rewriting breaks cert validation.

Suggested internal change to runbook (short):
- Add a troubleshooting section: curl -v --resolve api.control.redwood.com:443:34.202.10.12 https://api.control.redwood.com/health returns 200 and cert CN=api.control.redwood.com.
- Include example proxy config for common proxies (NGINX, Squid, F5 BIG-IP) showing preserve SNI and pass-through config.

Laura — can you confirm legal/contract treatment of pinned egress IP as an add-on? I'll prep a brief bullet for commercial.

-Jordan

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
To: Nicole Rojas <nicole@greenwave.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Aug 2026 09:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private endpoint: outbound connectivity and TLS interception concerns

Nicole — following up with the attachments again and a short mutual action plan (MAP):

MAP (proposed)
- Day 0–3: GreenWave opens the three control-plane IPV4 addresses and two artifact CIDRs in test environment; enable SNI passthrough for api.control.redwood.com.
- Day 4: Redwood will run a controlled smoke test against GreenWave test proxy (we'll provide a test cert if you cannot expose SNI).
- Day 5–10: Confirm artifact fetches and telemetry stability; document any TLS inspection issues.
- Signoff: Production cutover after successful smoke test and security acceptance.

We are fine to provide a signed manifest for the IP set rotation and can lock a customer-specific NAT for enterprise customers under contract. If you prefer, we can also ship a small VM appliance image for an outbound bastion that we certify (this removes the need for you to maintain rules for artifact CIDRs).

Please let me know which option you prefer and a couple of time slots for a 30-minute technical gating call this week.

Regards,
Tessa
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Attachments: bastion-proxy-arch.png, egress-ip-list.csv, egress-runbook-v1.pdf
